decision: named the cause in the code: serve_until_stopped spawned the bus before running required recovery, so a peer that connects when the socket appears can submit into the session the pass is unwinding, and two settlements of one execution make a history no reader can replay

result: the failure is the symptom; the ordering is the defect

decision: moved required recovery above the bus spawn, and landed a test that seeds 24 crashed sessions, starts the daemon, and asserts nothing is left in flight at the first moment a peer can connect
why: fixing the ordering removes the race at its source rather than making the test retry, and the test is falsifiable: with the old ordering restored it fails reporting 4 sessions in flight
result: falsified on the old ordering, green on the new; the relay test passes 10 of 10 where it failed 2 of 2

decision: denied TCP to every workload by handling AccessNet::from_all(ABI::V4) with no network rule, with the Linux 6.7 floor named in the refusal
why: a model-driven shell with unrestricted dialling is the rounds largest hole, and Landlock can close TCP even though it cannot close UDP or AF_UNIX
